title: Ranks and memory
description: Each machine: every app's rank, what that rank may do, what the app is, the memory it books and its real memory over the last 24 hours.

options.content:
| Rank | Number | Can push out lower ranks to start? | Can be pushed out by | What it is for |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `system-node-critical` | 2,000,001,000 | yes | nothing | k3s's own plumbing. |
| `system-cluster-critical` | 2,000,000,000 | yes | nothing | Cluster essentials: names, the web front door, GitOps. |
| `homelab-critical` | 1,000,000 | yes | k3s's own | Keep running: camera recordings, websites, the lab sites, monitoring. |
| `homelab-normal` | 100,000 | yes | `homelab-critical`, k3s's own | Services with no tag. |
| `batch-high` | 30,000 | no, waits for room | `homelab-critical`, `homelab-normal`, k3s's own | Free Motion's browsers and website helper, hourly or daily jobs whose results are expected (rating, cat monitor, the archiver). |
| `batch-make-room` | 25,000 | yes | `homelab-critical`, `homelab-normal`, k3s's own | Short daily jobs that may stop lower pods (the mail classifier) to start: cat flash, BoardGameFinder. |
| `steps-aside` | 22,000 | no, waits for room | `homelab-critical`, `homelab-normal`, `batch-make-room`, k3s's own | Services that give their room to batch-make-room jobs and come back after: the mail classifier. |
| `batch-mid` | 20,000 | no, waits for room | `homelab-critical`, `homelab-normal`, `batch-make-room`, k3s's own | Long jobs that resume where they stopped (Whisper, speakers). |
| `batch-low` | 10,000 | no, waits for room | `homelab-critical`, `homelab-normal`, `batch-make-room`, k3s's own | Jobs that retry on their own, idle helpers (downloads, shell). |
| `(none)` | 0 | no, waits for room | `homelab-critical`, `homelab-normal`, `batch-make-room`, k3s's own | Pods made before the default rank existed; they get homelab-normal at their next restart. |

**Two separate rules.** *Getting in:* a pod starts only where its **booking** fits; a rank marked yes may stop pods of a strictly lower number on that machine to make room, the others wait. *Running out of real memory:* ranks don't count; the kernel kills the biggest containers first (a small booking makes it likelier), and a container above its own limit is killed whatever its rank.
